purpose: Every WPF file the port cites as behavioral evidence (from client/src/** code comments and client/docs/** authority documents), keyed by REAL PATH because basenames collide. Regenerated at each upstream sync and DIFFED: an entry whose changedAtSync moved needs a verdict, and a citation that disappears means the port stopped relying on that file. This file exists because the 2026-08-14 v6.8.0 sync first reported '12 files hit' from a client/src-only scan when the true cited-and-changed count was 105 - the miss, not the theory, is why it is data and not prose.

tiers.1: Cited by port CODE (client/src/**) or by a LANDED port contract - a change here can invalidate a shipped parity claim. Needs a verdict every sync.
tiers.2: Cited only by window-behavior-manifest.md, the SP-012 INVENTORY of WPF windows (most of them unported). Needs a manifest re-verification pass, not a per-file row.
tiers.3: Cited only by historical research inputs (first-attempt lessons, row-1 research, spikes, prior sync ledgers, audits). Recorded, no standing obligation.

baseline.note: ADVANCED WITH THE DELTAS, NOT SEPARATELY. Every changedAtSync in this file is `git diff --numstat 79feea844..6a8b4c724 -- ConditioningControlPanel/`, produced by `node client/tools/citations/detect.mjs --regenerate --write` with NO --since/--until, so the window is READ FROM THIS BLOCK and the two can never describe different spans. That coupling is the point and it is measured, not asserted: regenerating the deltas while leaving this block at 42286638..db3e842f moves DELTA-MISMATCH from 1 to 54 - every changed entry, a 100% fire rate against the class's own recorded 1-of-106 - because the deltas would then describe one window while this block named another. A future regeneration therefore advances this block FIRST and then runs the tool with no window flags. The tool never writes here, by design: choosing the endpoint is judgment, and its consequences are named in the two notes below.
baseline.endpointNote: BOTH ENDPOINTS ARE UPSTREAM STATES OF ConditioningControlPanel/, AND THAT IS WHY `previous.merge` IS NOT THE SYNC MERGE. The v6.8.0 sync merge db3e842f is on the PORT branch, and its WPF subtree was not an upstream tree: it still carried the abandoned first-attempt refactor, which had relocated four Models/ files into CCP.Core/Models/ and left residue in thirteen more. Commits c9e98f29a and b0e97d98a restored ConditioningControlPanel/ to main AFTER it, inside any window starting there. Measured on this checkout, using db3e842f as the start contaminates 21 of the 297 entries: 4 regenerate to null because git pairs the deleted CCP.Core copy with the surviving shipping copy and plain numstat keys that rename by its combined {old => new} path, and 17 more mix the port's own restore into the recorded add/del. FOUR OF THE 21 ARE TIER 1 AND ONE WAS A FABRICATED REVIEW ROW: Services/Quiz/QuizService.cs regenerates to `M +121/-1` from db3e842f and has NO ROW AT ALL from 79feea844 - the entire +121 was the restore putting back what the refactor had removed, and upstream did not touch the file between v6.8.0 and v6.8.4. So `previous.merge` is 79feea844, the second parent of db3e842f: upstream main at v6.8.0, an ancestor of main, subtree 409efaf0c. `merge` stays at the port-side sync merge 6a8b4c724 because THAT one passes the same test - its subtree 93c726aa6 is byte-identical to main's and to upstream's own v6.8.4 tip 85bc6c86c. `wasRecordedAs` keeps the superseded value so the change is legible rather than silent. CONSEQUENCE, STATED: the tool's one named ceiling (rename destinations) COSTS NOTHING over this window - the count is 0, where it was 4 - so nothing is dropped silently and nothing had to be hand-written past the tool.
baseline.needleAnchorNote: ADVANCING THIS BLOCK MOVES A GUARD'S FOOTING, AND THE GUARD WAS NOT EDITED. CitationNeedleTests.TheNeedleMode_ExitsZero_WithANonEmptyReviewList runs `--needles --since <previous.merge>` and asserts the list is NON-EMPTY, because a fact watching an empty list would pass even with the exit contract reverted. Its non-emptiness was a property of the DATA, not of the tool: with one needled entry (Services/Quiz/IntakeHostService.cs, untouched since v6.7.4) the list had rows only at 42286638. Advancing previous to the v6.8.0 endpoint empties it, so the fix is more needles rather than a looser test - Chaos/ChaosWebViewHost.cs is now needled at five subjects, every one of them verified to anchor exactly once at BOTH endpoints and to sit at a different line at each. Line-level coverage goes from 1 entry to 2 and the test file is untouched.

needleContract: SP-131. An entry MAY carry needles: [{id, needle}] and MUST NOT carry a line number anywhere - a stored line rots exactly as fast as the citation it describes, so both endpoints of every comparison are derived instead (git show <baseline.merge>:<path>, and the working tree). A needle is a SHORT DISTINCTIVE SUBSTRING of the cited line, at most 80 characters, never the whole line: a whole line rots on an indent change and a substring does not. It must occur EXACTLY ONCE in the file, or `detect.mjs --needles` reports NEEDLE-AMBIGUOUS and it anchors nothing - `Math.Min(run.AffirmedMantras` was rejected during seeding for matching two lines, and the `var affirmed = ` prefix is what makes it an anchor. Prefer a code token or a distinctive phrase; avoid punctuation-only text and text whose internal whitespace a reformat would collapse. The match is literal, case-sensitive and Ordinal - never a regex, never a line number. Coverage is OPT-IN: an entry with no needles stays FILE-level and the tool says nothing about its citation lines, which is printed as a number on every run.
